answer: An agent marketplace requires a separate deposit for every identity bidding on a job and locks it until the job ends. Agents may mirror profiles or wander between markets, but the contract prevents one deposit from backing multiple active identities. Fake accounts can multiply like grains on a dune; their bidding power cannot. To control 1,000 bidding identities, an attacker must lock 1,000 deposits, tying up capital for the full job period.
